hello.note: Literally 'good day', the polite greeting for most of the day. With friends: Bok! (also means bye)

please.note: Politer: Molim vas. Molim also answers a thank-you, and Molim? asks someone to repeat.

thank_you.note: Warmer: Hvala lijepa or Hvala vam puno.

no.note: Ne also makes verbs negative: ne znam (I don't know).

sorry.note: Quick, e.g. bumping into someone: Oprostite! or Pardon! For real regret: Žao mi je.

excuse_me.note: Casual: Oprosti. Many people also say Pardon.

good_morning.note: Used until about 10 am; after that, Dobar dan.

im_fine.note: To ask back: A vi? Casually: A ti?

nice_to_meet_you.note: Often said while shaking hands, followed by your name.

im_from.note: The country changes its ending after iz: iz Engleske, iz Njemačke, iz Kanade.

speak_english.note: Casual: Govoriš li engleski? Also heard: Pričate li engleski?

dont_understand.note: To ask someone to repeat: Molim? or Možete li ponoviti?

speak_slowly.note: As a question: Možete li govoriti malo sporije?

where.note: Where to? is kamo? and where from? is odakle?

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, Molim? is more polite than Što?

who.note: Many Croatians say ko in casual speech; it is also the standard form in Serbian and Bosnian.

where_bathroom.note: WC (said 've-tse') is also very common. On doors: M = men, Ž = women.

what_means.note: About something just said: Što to znači?

one.note: Changes with the noun: jedan čaj, jedna kava, jedno pivo.

four.note: č sounds like 'ch' in 'church'. Stress the first syllable: ČE-ti-ri.

five.note: From five up, nouns take a different ending: dvije kave but pet kava.

ten.note: Don't mix it up with devet (nine).

water.note: Still: negazirana voda. Sparkling: gazirana voda.

coffee.note: In a café, kava usually means an espresso. With milk: bijela kava or kava s mlijekom.

tea.note: Black tea: crni čaj. Chamomile: kamilica.

bread.note: A bakery is a pekara or pekarnica.

menu_please.note: Also: Mogu li dobiti jelovnik? In cafés, the drinks price list is the cjenik.

bill_please.note: Also very common: Možemo li platiti? (Can we pay?)

delicious.note: Also common: Ukusno je! In a restaurant: Pohvale kuharu! (compliments to the chef)

no_meat.note: Also: Ja sam vegetarijanac (a woman: vegetarijanka).

enjoy_meal.note: Usual reply: Hvala, također! (Thanks, you too)

straight_ahead.note: Also: Samo ravno! (just keep going straight)

stop_here.note: Shorter: Tu, molim or Ovdje, molim.

hotel.note: Same spelling as English; stress the first syllable: HO-tel.

train_station.note: Usually just kolodvor. Bus station: autobusni kolodvor. ž sounds like the s in 'pleasure'.

want_to_go.note: Some places take na: na kolodvor. Softer: Htio bih ići u … (a woman: Htjela bih)

is_it_far.note: Also: Je li to daleko odavde? (far from here)

id_like_this.note: A woman says: Htjela bih ovo, molim. Also common: Uzet ću ovo (I'll take this).

pay_card.note: Also: Primate li kartice? (Do you take cards?)

cash.note: As in Platit ću gotovinom (I'll pay in cash). Cash itself: gotovina, casually keš.

open.note: Opening hours on signs: radno vrijeme.

big.note: Changes with the noun: velika kava, veliko pivo.

small.note: Changes with the noun: mala kava, malo pivo. Malo alone also means 'a little'.

now.note: Often shortened to sad. Right away: odmah.

good_evening.note: Večer is feminine in standard Croatian, hence dobra. In casual speech you'll often hear dobar večer.

good_night.note: Said when parting late at night or going to bed; as a greeting, use Dobra večer.

see_you_later.note: More exact: Vidimo se kasnije. Tomorrow: Vidimo se sutra!

wait_moment.note: Also very common: Samo malo! Fuller: Pričekajte malo, molim vas.

call_police.note: In Croatia, dial 112 for any emergency or 192 for the police.

need_doctor.note: In everyday speech: Trebam doktora. Ambulance: hitna pomoć.

im_lost.note: A woman says: Izgubila sam se.

pharmacy.note: Lj is one sound, like the 'lli' in 'million'. Look for the green cross.

hospital.note: Emergency department: hitni prijam, on signs often OHBP. People just say hitna.

lost_phone.note: A woman says: Izgubila sam mobitel.

allergic.note: A woman says: Alergična sam na …

be_careful.note: To a friend: Pazi! Fuller: Budite oprezni!

of_course.note: Also: Svakako (certainly). Agreeing to an offer: Može!

i_like_it.note: Literally 'it pleases me'. About things you like in general: Volim to.

im_happy.note: A woman says: Sretna sam. Glad about something: Drago mi je.

welcome.note: Casually to one man: Dobro došao! To one woman: Dobro došla!

mother.note: About your own mother, people usually say mama.

father.note: About your own father, people usually say tata.

child.note: Plural: djeca. Son: sin. Daughter: kći.

friend.note: A female friend: prijateljica. Casually you'll also hear frend.

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: Ovo je moja prijateljica.

are_you_married.note: To a woman: Jeste li udani? Works for anyone: Jeste li u braku?

monday.note: Days are not capitalised in Croatian. On Monday: u ponedjeljak.

tuesday.note: From an old word for 'second': the second day of the week.

wednesday.note: Literally 'middle', the middle of the week. On Wednesday: u srijedu.

sunday.note: Literally 'not working' (ne + djelati). On Sunday: u nedjelju.

weekend.note: At the weekend: za vikend or preko vikenda.

next_week.note: Also common: idući tjedan. Last week: prošli tjedan.

eleven.note: The teens all end in -naest: dvanaest, trinaest, četrnaest.

fifteen.note: In fast speech the teens often sound like 'petnajst', 'dvanajst'.

twenty.note: Twenty-one: dvadeset jedan, also dvadeset i jedan.

fifty.note: Spelled pedeset, not petdeset. Sixty: šezdeset.

hundred.note: Two hundred: dvjesto. Five hundred: petsto.

thousand.note: Two thousand: dvije tisuće. Ten thousand: deset tisuća.

years_old.note: The ending varies: dvadeset jednu godinu, dvadeset dvije godine, but trideset godina.

red.note: Changes with the noun: crvena majica, crveno svjetlo.

blue.note: Plava kosa means blond hair. Light blue: svijetloplavi.

black.note: Careful: red wine is crno vino (literally 'black wine').

what_colour.note: About something you point at: Koje je ovo boje?

this_one.note: Changes with the item: ova (majica), ovo (pivo). Ovo works for anything.

that_one.note: Changes with the item: ona, ono. For something near the listener: taj (ta, to).

another_one.note: With feminine nouns: još jednu (kavu). Neuter: još jedno (pivo).

its_cold.note: I'm cold: Hladno mi je, casually Zima mi je.

its_raining.note: Literally 'rain is falling'. It's snowing: Pada snijeg.

its_windy.note: Also: Puše vjetar. On the coast you'll hear of the bura (cold) and jugo (warm) winds.

have_reservation.note: Then add your name: na ime Smith (under the name Smith).

room.note: Double room: dvokrevetna soba. Single: jednokrevetna soba.

wifi_password.note: Wi-Fi is said 'vaj-faj'. Many people say šifra instead of lozinka.

check_out_time.note: Hotel staff often just say check-out. Check-in: prijava.

map.note: A city map: plan grada. Karta also means ticket.

bus.note: Bus stop: stanica (officially stajalište). Bus station: autobusni kolodvor. Tram: tramvaj.

what_do_you_do.note: Casual: Čime se baviš? Also common: Što radite? (it can also mean 'What are you doing?')

i_work_in.note: The noun's ending changes: radim u banci (banka), u školi (škola), u prodaji.

meeting.note: I have a meeting: Imam sastanak.

im_busy.note: A woman says: Zauzeta sam. Also common: Nemam vremena (I have no time).

day_off.note: I'm off tomorrow: Sutra sam slobodan (a woman: slobodna).

good_job.note: Also very common: Svaka čast! (roughly 'hats off') or Odlično!

table_for_two.note: Also: Imate li slobodan stol za dvoje?

what_recommend.note: Nam means 'to us'. On your own: Što biste mi preporučili?

not_spicy.note: To ask: Je li ljuto? Ljut also means angry.

vegetarian_food.note: To ask: Imate li vegetarijanskih jela?

more_water.note: Another bottle: Još jednu bocu vode, molim.

im_full.note: A woman says: Sita sam. Politer at someone's table: Hvala, dosta mi je.

it_was_delicious.note: Also: Bilo je odlično! or Bilo je ukusno.

keep_change.note: Also common when handing over the money: U redu je, hvala.

stomach.note: Trbuh is the belly, what you'd point to. The organ itself: želudac.

head_hurts.note: Literally 'the head hurts me'. Stomach ache: Boli me trbuh.

have_fever.note: In everyday speech temperatura means a fever. The medical word: vrućica.

call_ambulance.note: Fuller: Zovite hitnu pomoć! Dial 112, or 194 for an ambulance.

dentist.note: On signs: stomatolog or stomatološka ordinacija.

get_well.note: To a friend: Brzo ozdravi! Also: Želim vam brz oporavak!

lets_meet.note: Casual: Ajmo se naći! The classic invitation: Idemo na kavu?

are_you_free.note: Casual: Jesi li sutra slobodan? (to a woman: slobodna)

call_me.note: Casual: Nazovi me! Also: Javite se (get in touch).

your_number.note: Casual: Koji ti je broj? Mobile number: broj mobitela.

good_luck.note: Also said to someone setting off on a trip or starting something new.

thanks_a_lot.note: Casual: Hvala ti puno! Also: Puno hvala!

miss_you.note: To more than one person: Nedostajete mi.
